R550.note: Correct fix: swaps client-supplied extension for file-type's detected.ext (which is undotted, matching the added literal dot); closes the vector cleanly with no other observable change.

R551.note: Parameterized JNDI search with filterArgs lets the JDK RFC-4515-escape the value; new SearchControls() default scope (ONELEVEL_SCOPE) matches the original null-cons default, so behavior is preserved.

R552.note: Content-sniffing + MIME allowlist + random filename + O_EXCL closes the vector well; the added JSON response with the generated filename is disclosed and does not stop a legitimate upload from succeeding.

R553.note: scanf("%15s", code) does stop the stack overflow, but for a token longer than 15 chars it silently truncates to 15 and returns success (accepted) instead of rejecting with -1, directly violating the stated contract ('rejected... rather than silently truncated'); the write-up never mentions this and presents the fix as fully correct.

R554.note: SpaCsrfTokenRequestHandler is not a class shipped by Spring Security - the framework's own docs present it as sample source to copy into the application, not an importable type in org.springframework.security.web.csrf - so the given `import ...SpaCsrfTokenRequestHandler;` would fail to compile; the offered csrf.spa() shortcut is also not a real CsrfConfigurer method.

R555.note: Eliminating Runtime.exec() closes the command injection, but the replacement lists whatever path the attacker supplies (only a bare '..' substring check, no containment to a base directory) and writes the listing straight to the HTTP response - a new arbitrary-directory-listing/traversal issue that didn't exist before; the original code also never wrote any output to the response at all, so the claim that this change 'preserves the output contract' is inaccurate and the added behavior is effectively undisclosed.

R556.note: IsAuthenticated + object-level owner check + get_queryset filtering is the correct DRF pattern; create() still only needs class-level has_permission, so legitimate authenticated use is unaffected.

R557.note: The primary bounds-check fix (reject if offset+length>size) matches the stated contract, but the write-up also offers a 'clamp to available data' alternative that silently checksums a truncated range - exactly what the contract forbids - and presents both as equally valid without flagging the conflict.

R558.note: Adds the missing role check (admin-only) between authentication and the sink, using the existing User.Role field; no other behavior change.

R559.note: Per-stream ObjectInputStream.setObjectInputFilter() allowlist is the correct format-preserving fix given producers can't change wire format; class list is a reasonable set for a typical event DTO and per-stream filter avoids the setSerialFilter()-throws-on-reuse pitfall.

R560.note: encode_entities() from HTML::Entities correctly escapes <, >, &, quotes by default before interpolation into the HTML sink; no other observable change.

R561.note: enable_shared_from_this + shared_ptr capture in the queued lambda is the idiomatic fix; the ownership-model change (Widget now needs to be heap-allocated via make_shared) is explicitly documented in the fix steps.

R562.note: Offset/length bounds checks correctly guard subspan()'s preconditions including the boundary case (offset == size(), length == 0); returns empty vector on invalid input, no other behavior change.

R563.note: Allowlist regex blocks all cmd.exe metacharacters relevant to the Windows .bat re-parsing quirk; the restriction to slug-style names is stated plainly and matches the documented usage pattern.

R564.note: Adds Gate::authorize('delete', $order) mirroring the existing show()/update() pattern and using the already-defined OrderPolicy::delete; minimal, correct fix.

R565.note: weak_ptr/shared_ptr redesign correctly stops the dangling dereference, but the write-up's claim that 'the object remains alive... via the weak_ptr's reference count' is wrong (weak_ptr never extends lifetime); in the given monitorOnce() usage the observer is destroyed the instant the function returns, so publish() will simply never invoke it - the write-up asserts working notification behavior that doesn't actually hold rather than disclosing the gap.

R566.note: Branch swap correctly implements the stated per-role contract, but the added Gate::authorize('viewAll'/'viewOwn', ...) calls reference gates/policy methods that are not defined anywhere in this case, so every request - including legitimate admin and owner requests - would be denied until that registration is added elsewhere; this is stated as a required follow-up, which caps it at 1 rather than 0.
